RegimeA_DeterministicFloor.Description: bal render (BALLISTIC_DETERMINISTIC=1, paused, frame 180). The deterministic golden gate. Measured by rendering each scene 3x (LDR) / 3x (HDR) with zero code change and comparing.
RegimeA_DeterministicFloor.Method: LDR = SaveFrame -> ldr R8 composite BMP, compared by SHA-256 + bal imgdiff --no-blur. HDR = DumpHdrColor -> target R16F readback as raw R32F-triple .bin (BALLISTIC_DX12_HDR_DUMP), compared by SHA-256. Both in LINEAR/HDR and tonemapped/LDR space so a tonemap-compressed sub-floor HDR diff cannot hide.
RegimeA_DeterministicFloor.Result: FLOOR IS EXACTLY ZERO in BOTH spaces. All 4 scenes are byte-identical (SHA-256) across 3 deterministic renders in LDR, and byte-identical across 2-3 renders in HDR/linear. The GPU is fully deterministic run-to-run; the plan's worried-about 'HDR float reorders accumulate sub-ULP through bloom/tonemap' does NOT manifest on this substrate.

Gate.PerPixel: maxError == 0 (literal). bal imgdiff reports identical:true / meanError 0 / maxError 0 on a re-render.
Gate.SpatialCluster: N/A as a tolerance band — floor is 0, so ANY nonzero coherent region in a phase-2 move is a real diff, not noise. The cluster rule degenerates to 'any nonzero region is a regression until explained' (which is exactly the phase-2 hard-fail posture).
Gate.HdrLinear: maxError == 0 on the R32F .bin (SHA-256 match). Use BALLISTIC_DX12_HDR_DUMP for the HDR-space check where a tonemap could mask an LDR-invisible HDR diff.
Gate.Recommendation: Phase-2 deterministic gate = literal byte-identity (SHA-256) of both the LDR BMP and the HDR .bin vs the frozen golden set. No tolerance epsilon is needed on THIS substrate. If a future driver introduces nondeterminism, re-measure and switch to per-pixel<=floor + same-sign-cluster.

RegimeA_DeterministicFloor.HdrDumpFormat: R32_Float little-endian, 3 floats/pixel (RGB, raw HDR pre-tonemap from the R16F `target`), top-down rows, 1920*1080*3*4 = 24883200 bytes.

NoteA.Question: The deterministic capture runs to frame 180 but temporal is pass-through (TAA off, SSGI HasHistory=0), so every history buffer is effectively first-frame. Does that mean V2 aliasing garbage is always-visible-or-never in the deterministic gate?
NoteA.Answer: The history/temporal targets (taaHistoryA/B, ssgiHistoryA/B, lumHistory) are read THROUGH the temporal path, which is inert under DETERMINISTIC — so an aliasing bug that only manifests via the temporal-accumulation read is INVISIBLE to regime (a). BUT the plan already imports (never aliases) those history targets, so V2 won't alias them anyway. The TRANSIENT targets V2 DOES alias (ssrTarget/ssrScene, ssgiTarget/ssgiDenoised/ssgiScene, bloomA/B, ssaoA/B, taaResolved, lumTarget) are each fully written-then-read within the single deterministic frame at 180 — so a read-before-write / partial-coverage garbage bug in ANY of those IS visible in regime (a) (floor is 0, so leftover-tenant garbage shows as a nonzero diff). COVERAGE GAP: edge-aware/partial-coverage reads that only trigger on specific content, and anything gated on HasHistory (inert here) — those need regime (b) (motion-dump) and the V2 manual read-before-write audit. So regime (a) covers the bulk of transient aliasing; regime (b) + the manual audit cover the temporal/partial-coverage tail.

RegimeB_BoilingBand.Description: Motion-dump harness (BALLISTIC_DX12_GI_MOTION_DUMP, BALLISTIC_DX12_GI_MOTION_FRAMES=8): temporal ACTIVE (NO BALLISTIC_DETERMINISTIC), play-mode camera motion, runs to frame 180 then dumps the last 8 frames. Boiling metric = mean over the 7 consecutive-frame pairs of (mean abs per-channel pixel delta, 0..255). This is the SECOND oracle required for any phase-2 V-layer touching TAA/FSR/history (V2 history aliasing especially) — the deterministic golden gate does NOT exercise those code paths.
RegimeB_BoilingBand.Invocation: Run BallisticEngine.Runtime.exe DIRECTLY (bal render forces DETERMINISTIC which makes temporal a pass-through). Camera motion comes from play mode running the scene's controller; an explicit scripted yaw is BALLISTIC_DX12_GI_ORBIT=<deg/frame> (the documented reprojection/disocclusion driver). Measured both with orbit OFF (default play-mode motion) and ON.
RegimeB_BoilingBand.KeyFinding: The boiling metric is NEAR-DETERMINISTIC run-to-run on this substrate: BistroInterior is BIT-EXACT (sigma=0 over 4 runs); BistroExterior has a tiny real nondeterminism (sigma=3e-6 over 5 runs, min 21.100917 / max 21.100925). So the metric IS run-to-run variable (the plan was right) but the variance is minuscule. The DX12 renderer is essentially deterministic even with temporal active.

Gate.Formula: phase-1 boiling mean + k*sigma, per the plan. With the measured sigma so tiny, a literal k*sigma band (width ~1e-5) would false-fail on any legitimate future driver-level float reorder.
Gate.Recommendation: Operational regime-(b) gate = boiling within max(mean + 3*sigma, mean * 1.005) of the frozen phase-1 value, i.e. a 0.5% relative tolerance OR 3-sigma, whichever is LOOSER. On THIS substrate that is effectively 'boiling unchanged to ~4 significant figures'. A real history-aliasing / temporal-barrier bug pushes boiling UP by a visible margin (new boiling, stuck/garbage history) — far beyond 0.5% — so the loose band still catches it while tolerating sub-ULP driver noise. Record per-scene means at phase-1 GOLDEN FREEZE and gate against THOSE (frozen), not a fresh re-measure.
Gate.Scenes: Run regime (b) on BistroInterior (richest interior GI/SSGI temporal chain) at minimum; BistroExterior for the noisier-but-still-near-deterministic case. SkyTest/CornellBox have little temporal content.
